questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since I study French at the university in Copenhagen, for me France was the best option, and I always had a dream about studying at the Sorbonne University, all though it disappointed me a lot.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really didn't find my experience at the Sorbonne University good. First of all, there was an enormous lack of communication, lack of understanding, lack of help, etc. The main problem this semester, was not having access to the school system "moodle". There is no it-support office, so we to multiple office(s), people, teachers, administration, wrote so many mails regarding this problem, but no replies.  So no-one tried to help, therefore our coordinator from Denmark had to get involved, and suddenly, there was help to get. We got access to moodle after 10 weeks, the semester is 13 weeks. Due to not being able to enter moodle, also means, you dont have access to the documents, homework, powerpoints, overview of the semester, exams, all of the important stuff. Furthermore during my periode, my personal life was a mess, during the exam-period, I was apartment scammed, my boyfriend and I broke up, due to unfaithfulness, we had a death in my family, but I was told, I had to do the exams, and there was nothing to do, even though I didn't feel well with my mental health. During our exams, we could only bring a French-french dictionary. which is a very high demand, when you are only an exchange student. Plus the level of French was beyond B2, and if I remember correctly, we discovered the UFR (bachelor) they assigned us, was on a C1 level, which didn't match the requirements, we were suppose to fulfil. There was in general much confusing among the Erasmus students, and we where told different information, and didn't feel like, there was anyone to bring our concerns to. I also tried to ask one of my teachers regarding an exam, because we didn't know what to do, and he never even responded. Some of the courses expected that the reading materiel was read before the semester, how should we have a clue about that? This school is beyond inattentive regarding exchange students. The don't care. Furthermore, the wifi is non-existing and during winter it is super cold, since the school is old, and always charge your laptop at home, because they don't have plugs in all rooms.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It wasn't easy at all to find the schedules and the courses to follow was a jungle to put it mildly. Also I missed some classes, not being able to orientate myself at the school, we didn't even receive a map.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was some info meetings, 1/2 was helpful. The first was the coordinators, that enlightened us about, absence, courses etc. The second, was more "social" so to speak, which is also okay, but it would have been more helpful to have meetings regarding the grading system, how to do the specific assignments, because they do assignment in a way different maner, a tour around the school would have been great, how exams functions, how to get access to the library, etc.

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Really difficult, there are so many scammers.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be careful, and if they have the opportunity go to the city and check the apartment out before hand, and meet the renter.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I tried to apply for a housing, but there was limited spots, which makes sense, but what didn't make sense, was that it depended on what your parents income, and I am not depended on their money, so I was not able to get one.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process is very long, but fair I think. The documents, that CPH University requires are okay, but they were difficult to find from Sorbonne, that made it hard.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to apply, do plenty of paperwork, get a pre-approval etc, make sure you have your insurance in order, european healthcard

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: help? haha, none.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: fine

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Seek help, from people who previously went to the school

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Could have been more diversed. But overall okay.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: High level of French, which was beyond what was expected from our level of French. The B2 level is a low demand in concerns to how the courses are taught, especially regarding the exams as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite boring, but that's the culture clash. We often sat and listened for 2/3 hours without a break. There is often not a powerpoint or anything, so it is basically just a professor speaking for two hours, and you sit and listen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Rhetorical devices, law, grammar, literature and a media and technic course.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Law and grammar

questions.answer: The lack of administrations, communication, the arrogance, the distance between students and teachers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be sure you have a very high level of French, C1 is best. B2 is too difficult to keep up.
2) Be consistent, if you need help and don't take no for an answer
3) Be aware that this is a high level, and not something where you can slack

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the library, there are no reading halls. The wifi is non-existing, almost not any plugs, som make sure your laptop is charged.
